extraction.name: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
extraction.description: This work presents the first systematic study on object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). It evaluates several representative LVLMs on the MSCOCO dataset, finding that they suffer from severe object hallucination, particularly for objects that frequently appear or co-occur in visual instruction datasets. The paper proposes POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation), a stable and flexible method for evaluating object hallucination by converting the task into a binary classification problem.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.citeAs: Li, Y., Du, Y., Zhou, K., Wang, J., Zhao, W. X., & Wen, J. R. (2023). Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2305.10355.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The study uses the MSCOCO dataset, specifically sampling 2,000 images with annotations from its validation set. The data collection involves evaluating existing LVLMs on this pre-existing dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MSCOCO (Lin et al., 2014) validation set, specifically 2,000 images with annotations about contained objects and human-labeled captions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The study randomly sampled 2,000 images from the MSCOCO validation set that had more than 3 ground-truth objects in the annotations. For POPE evaluation, questions were constructed based on ground-truth objects and negative sampling strategies (Random, Popular, Adversarial).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset relies on existing human-annotated object labels from MSCOCO. For the POPE method, ground-truth objects are extracted from these annotations or via automatic segmentation tools (SEEM). Questions are formulated as 'Is there a <object> in the image?' with answers 'Yes' or 'No' based on the presence of the object.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEEM (Zou et al., 2023) is used as an automatic segmentation tool to annotate images for POPE evaluation on unannotated datasets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Object hallucination hinders the safe use of LVLMs in real-world deployment, potentially leading to unexpected consequences (e.g., in autonomous driving). The work aims to improve reliability and human-alignment of LVLMs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: LVLMs are prone to hallucinate objects that frequently appear or co-occur in the visual instruction datasets (e.g., MSCOCO). The evaluation shows that hallucination rates correlate with object frequency and co-occurrence in the training/instruction data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The study only focuses on object hallucination, not other aspects of LVLM capacity. Results are based on a subset of the validation set due to computational constraints. POPE relies on matching-based methods which may fail if models do not explicitly output 'Yes'/'No'. The study compared a small number of LVLMs and did not include recently released or closed-source models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models. Testing and validating the stability and flexibility of the POPE evaluation metric.
